pillars.label: 真实科学发现
pillars.title: 从真实问题出发
pillars.body: 科学发现往往始于一个尚未被清晰定义的问题。我们从科学家面对的未知、瓶颈与异常现象出发，而不是从已经形式化的任务出发。

pillars.label: 真实反馈
pillars.title: 让数据与实验进入系统
pillars.body: 公开数据已经见底。模型真正缺的，是带有真实结果的科学数据。我们让真实的科学问题、数据与实验反馈进入下一代 AI 系统，让模型的输出接受数据、实验和专家判断的检验。

pillars.label: 参与发现
pillars.title: 从辅助科研，走向参与发现
pillars.body: 今天的 AI 可以检索文献、生成代码、处理数据。我们希望系统进入更完整的发现过程：识别未知、提出问题、修正假设、调用工具与实验，并在外部证据中更新判断。

dfm_teaser.title: 面向科学发现的研究范式
dfm_teaser.body: DFM（Discovery Foundation Models）不是一个单一模型，也不是要求所有系统按同一套流程运行的软件框架，而是 PhAI Labs 围绕 Discovery Intelligence 提出的一套研究范式、能力定义和系统组织方式。它通过形式化定义、流程图示、系统实例和真实科学案例，把“发现”从一个模糊概念具体化为一种可学习、可执行、可评测的模型系统能力。

items.tagline: 面向跨领域状态预测、干预模拟和科学诊断的统一科学世界模型

modules_teaser.note: ScienceBuddy、ScienceIDE 和 JEPA Anything 是三个完全独立的模块与研究方向，在产品形态、使用方式、论文和技术实现上彼此独立，不存在必须的调用或依赖关系。从未来愿景上看，三者可以形成一种可组合的研究路径：ScienceBuddy 通过科学家与智能体的交互收集反馈和研究轨迹；ScienceIDE 将这些数据和经验进一步组织为可复用的科学环境，用于任务执行、强化学习和模型训练；JEPA Anything 则探索对多个科学环境和干预结果进行统一的状态预测和模拟。这是一种未来可能的组合方式，不代表三者当前已经完成集成，也不改变它们各自独立的定位。

collab_teaser.title: 与科学家共同进入未知
collab_teaser.body: 首期重点关注生命科学与生物医学，同时面向化学、材料及其他前沿领域开放。我们寻找有明确科学问题的科学家、拥有高价值数据或实验环境的实验室、可以提供真实验证条件的湿实验团队，以及希望共同探索 DFM 的青年 PI、博士后和博士生。

hero.eyebrow: PhAI Labs · Toward real scientific discovery
hero.title: *AI* that participates in discovery
hero.subtitle: The third scaling law is scientific intelligence.
hero.lede: PhAI Labs works toward real scientific discovery: real scientific problems, data and experimental feedback enter next-generation AI systems, on a path from assisting research to taking part in discovery. DFM is the research paradigm we propose around Discovery Intelligence.
hero.kv_alt: PhAI Labs key visual: a network of particles
hero.program_note: “Apply now” opens the DFM Scientist Collaboration Program: we invite scientists, research groups and experimental platforms to bring real scientific questions, domain data and experimental feedback into DFM.

pillars.label: Real discovery
pillars.title: Start with real questions
pillars.body: Discovery begins with a question that is not yet well defined. We start from the unknowns, bottlenecks and anomalies scientists actually face, not from tasks that are already formalized.

pillars.label: Real feedback
pillars.title: Data and experiments enter the loop
pillars.body: Public data has run out. What models lack is scientific data with a real outcome attached. We bring real questions, data and experimental feedback into next-generation AI systems, and let model outputs face data, experiments and expert judgement.

pillars.label: Participating in discovery
pillars.title: From assisting to participating
pillars.body: AI can already retrieve literature, write code and process data. We want systems to enter the fuller process of discovery: identify unknowns, pose questions, revise hypotheses, run tools and experiments, and update their judgement against external evidence.

dfm_teaser.title: A research paradigm for discovery
dfm_teaser.body: DFM (Discovery Foundation Models) is neither a single model nor a software framework that forces every system through one pipeline. It is the research paradigm, capability definition and system organisation that PhAI Labs proposes around Discovery Intelligence: through formal definitions, process diagrams, system instances and real scientific cases, it turns “discovery” from a vague notion into a capability of model systems that can be learned, executed and evaluated.

modules_teaser.title: Three independent directions · released 16–18 September

items.name: ScienceBuddy · AI research partner
items.tagline: An interactive Scientific Agent, exploring RSI in RSI in real research interaction

items.name: ScienceIDE · science integrated development platform
items.tagline: A platform integrating scientific environments, code, tools and training pipelines

items.name: JEPA Anything · cross-domain unified science world model
items.tagline: A unified science world model for cross-domain state prediction, intervention simulation and scientific diagnosis

modules_teaser.note: ScienceBuddy, ScienceIDE and JEPA Anything are three fully independent modules and research directions: independent in product form, usage, papers and implementation, with no required calls or dependencies between them. Looking ahead, the three could form a composable research path: ScienceBuddy collects feedback and research trajectories from the interaction between scientists and agents; ScienceIDE organises that data and experience into reusable scientific environments for task execution, reinforcement learning and model training; JEPA Anything explores unified state prediction and simulation across multiple scientific environments and interventions. That is a possible future combination, not an integration that exists today, and it does not change their independent standing.

collab_teaser.title: Bring your question into the loop
collab_teaser.body: The first cohort prioritizes life science and biomedicine, while remaining open to chemistry, materials and other frontier fields. We are looking for scientists with clear questions, laboratories with high-value data or experimental environments, wet-lab teams able to provide real-world validation, and early-career PIs, postdocs and PhD students who want to explore DFM with us.
